chain.label: FAA icing certification requirements did not address thin, rough ice
chain.trigger: existing flight test certification requirements for flight into icing conditions do not test the effects of thin, rough ice on or aft of an airplane's protected surfaces

chain.label: Inadequate stall warning margin in icing conditions
chain.trigger: the Cessna 560 airplane's stall warning system does not provide a warning in all icing conditions, including those conditions in which thin, rough ice can accumulate on the protected surfaces

caused_by.evidence: the Federal Aviation Administration's failure to establish adequate certification requirements for flight into icing conditions, which led to the inadequate stall warning margin provided by the airplane's stall warning system

chain.label: Icing approach procedures not emphasized or evaluated in training
chain.trigger: no specific instruction exists to evaluate a pilot's performance of the AFM procedures to increase the airspeed and operate the deice boots during approaches when ice is present on the wings

chain.label: Descent through freezing drizzle and SLD icing; thin rough and residual ice on wings
chain.trigger: the airplane likely encountered SLD conditions from about 9,400 to 6,100 feet (the calculated altitude at which the upset occurred)

chain.label: Approach and missed approach briefing conducted late, while configuring and slowing
chain.trigger: although these airplane-handling tasks were being performed, the flight crew was concurrently briefing the ILS 26R approach

chain.label: Crew flew uncorrected Vref of 96 knots despite visible residual ice
chain.trigger: the V should have been increased from 96 to 104 knots because of the icing conditions

caused_by.evidence: pilots could benefit from the reinforcement during training of the Cessna 560 AFM requirements to increase the airspeed and operate the deice boots during approaches when ice is present on the wings
the flight crew did not increase the V while operating in icing conditions, contrary to company procedures and manufacturer guidance

chain.label: Deice boots not activated when configuring for approach and landing
chain.trigger: there is no evidence that the deice system was activated during the approach

caused_by.evidence: these procedures might not be getting emphasized during simulator training because the details of the training are left up to the individual instructors
when reconfiguring for approach and landing…with any ice accretion visible on the wing leading edge, regardless of thickness, activate the surface deice system
the briefing conducted late in the approach was a distraction that impeded the flight crew's ability to monitor and maintain airspeed and manage the deice system

chain.label: Crew failed to monitor and maintain airspeed as it decayed to about 90 knots
chain.trigger: The performance calculations and EGPWS ground speed data showed that the airspeed continued to decrease until the loss of control

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew's delayed approach briefing served to divert the pilots' attention from handling the airplane, managing the deice boot system, and monitoring the tasks that had to be performed during that period
According to company and manufacturer guidance on approach airspeeds in icing conditions, the airplane's airspeed at the time of the upset should have been about 114 knots

chain.label: Aerodynamic stall at about 90 knots with ice-contaminated wings
chain.trigger: the airplane entered a large roll to the left concurrent with a sudden decrease in pitch, indicating the start of the loss of control and aerodynamic stall

caused_by.evidence: the pilots' failure to activate the deice boots during the approach led to the continued accumulation of thin, rough ice on the protected surfaces, which can severely degrade an airplane's performance
the flight crew failed to maintain adequate airspeed during the final approach in icing conditions, which led to an aerodynamic stall

chain.label: Uncontrolled left roll to about 50 degrees bank with no recovery
chain.trigger: the airplane experienced an upset and the onset of a large roll to the left concurrent with a rapid decrease in pitch

caused_by.evidence: which caused an aerodynamic stall from which they did not recover
The CVR sound spectrum study indicated that the accident airplane's stall warning did not activate until after the stall

chain.label: Crash about 4 nm east of the runway; airplane destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: crashed about 4 nautical miles east of Pueblo Memorial Airport…the airplane was destroyed by impact forces and postcrash fire

caused_by.evidence: the last radar return was received at 0912:54 while the airplane was at an altitude of about 4,922 feet. One second later, the CVR stopped recording

chain.label: Two pilots and six passengers killed
chain.trigger: The two pilots and six passengers on board were killed

caused_by.evidence: the cause of death for the captain, first officer, and six passengers was "multiple traumatic injuries"
